sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Seelze, a town west of Hannover with the S-Bahn stations Seelze, Letter and Dedensen/Gümmer, steers parking policy mainly through planning, not through fees. We found no parking-fee or resident-parking by-law; the only parking entry in the town's by-law list is the repeal, decided on 28 January 2021, of the by-law that let builders pay a fee instead of providing parking spaces [2]. That is weak evidence, because the 2012 transport development plan already lists parking management and static parking guidance among the tools in use in Seelze, and calls for an adequate parking supply in the centre when the main street is redesigned [1]. The council adopted the integrated urban development concept ISEK 2035 on 25 April 2024 as a working basis. It sets goals to reduce the space used for parking in the town centres and give priority to walking and cycling, with planned measures including hubs at the three S-Bahn stations with car-sharing, a mobility hub with a carpool car park and a charging-expansion concept; these are intentions [8][9]. A traffic model for car traffic, built in October 2023 for the year 2035, tests housing and road scenarios and does not mention parking [6]. In March 2024 the town announced a six-month traffic trial in Seelze-Süd, a traffic-calmed zone where parking is allowed only on marked areas, and the page does not report its outcome [7]. From the 2026/27 school year, the town announced a bicycle street of about 150 metres near the Brüder-Grimm-Schule, with parent drop-off stops on parking bays [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The recent changes are at the stations and for charging. Two secured bike garages of 24 spaces each opened at Dedensen/Gümmer station on 30 April 2025, at a cost of about 175,000 euros, mostly federal money, and since 29 July 2026 they can be booked digitally, free of charge [10][13]. The cycling concept's final report of July 2025 counts 102 covered and 26 uncovered bike spaces at Letter station and 32 covered racks, 7 uncovered and a locked area with 72 racks at Seelze [11]. In July 2023 the town opened its first fast charger at Kastanienplatz in Letter, with about 200,000 euros, 80 percent, from a federal programme, and a post with two charge points at the Grand-Couronne-Allee car park opened on 28 July 2023; another post followed on Lange-Feld-Straße in Letter, in use since 9 September 2025 [4][5][12]. The Region Hannover installed sensors in 2021 at five pioneer park-and-ride sites, including Dedensen/Gümmer, with occupancy shown on the traffic management centre's website [3].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Deutsche Bahn lists three rail-station car parks in Seelze, open round the clock with no fee shown: Dedensen-Gümmer on Landschaftsstraße with 121 spaces, Seelze Bahnhof with 56 and Letter Bahnhof with 51 [15]. The Region's release of 2021 put Dedensen/Gümmer at 102 spaces [3], and an old transport plan, whose counts are undated, gave Seelze 93 spaces at 100 percent occupancy, Letter 51 at about 80 percent and Dedensen-Gümmer 121 at about 55 percent [0]. The ISEK says the stations have free park-and-ride spaces and free bicycle racks, which some users find often full or not secure [8].

Our data cover the Dedensen-Gümmer park-and-ride, whose feed gives 102 spaces, matching the Region's 2021 figure and not DB's 121, so the percentages are approximate. Over about 27 days since late September 2026 occupancy averaged about 17% on weekdays and 12% at weekends, with a peak of 32% around midday on a Thursday. The Seelze and Letter lots are not in our data.
